name: 6.2 The Central Limit Theorem for Sums
_note: Built 2026-08-12. All ten authored fresh (the bank had zero sums questions): q13-sum-notation, q14-sum-parameters, q15-sum-z-score, q16-sum-probability-greater, q17-sum-probability-less, q18-sum-probability-between, q19-sum-percentile, q20-sum-z-score-to-value, q21-sum-unit-conversion, pre-frq-grade-a-sum-interpretation. Points 10+10+10+10+10+10+10+9+9+12 = 100. BookSHelf 6.2 is the CLT for sums: Sigma X ~ N(n*mu, sqrt(n)*sigma), the z-score of a sum, probabilities and percentiles for a sum, and the unit-conversion habit. Pre-FRQ is authored-first (no sums FRQ to mirror; the CLT-reasoning mirror is claimed by 6.1's pre-FRQ): categories State the Sum's Parameters (3) / Compute the Probability or Percentile (5) / Interpret in Context (4), dropped category STATE THE SUM'S PARAMETERS.

questions.title: Sum Notation - the mean and standard deviation of Sigma X
The Parameters of the Sum - mu_SigmaX = n*mu and sigma_SigmaX = sqrt(n)*sigma
The z-Score of a Sum - z = (Sigma x - n*mu)/(sqrt(n)*sigma) and its sign-and-size reading
Probability That a Sum Is Greater Than a Value - P(Sigma x > c)
Probability That a Sum Is Less Than a Value - P(Sigma x < c)
Probability That a Sum Falls Between Two Values - P(lo < Sigma x < hi)
Percentile of the Sum - k for a sum, and its interpretation
Recover a Sum from a z-Score - s = n*mu + z*sqrt(n)*sigma and its sign-and-size reading
Unit Conversion for a Sum - minutes versus hours, and why it matters
Pre-FRQ Grade a Sum Interpretation - a sums scenario with a grading checklist, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
